summary: Bimal Krishna Matilal (1935–1991) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Central Calcutta College, University of Calcutta, Sanskrit College, and Harvard under Quine and Føllesdal. He held posts at Toronto (ca. 1968–1976) and Oxford (1976–1991).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha (1919–2002) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees from Patna University and SOAS, London, studying under Lionel David Barnett. His posts included Patna College, Patna University (Head from 1958), and K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute.

Bing Chen (b. 1945) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He served as a professor at Sichuan University from around 1987 and was attested as a professor at Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences in 1993.
Bintao Ma works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA from Peking University by 2008 and completed his PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xueyu (attested 2015).

Biraja Sankar Guha (1894–1961) was an anthropologist and Indologist who studied at Scottish Church College, Calcutta, and Harvard (PhD 1924). He directed the Anthropological Survey of India (1945–1954) and the Bihar Tribal Research Institute (1956–1959).

Birgit Kellner (b. 1969) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She completed her doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura. Her main posts include the University of Vienna (attested 2002–2011) and leadership of IKGA (attested 2017–2023).

Bisheshwar Nath Reu (1890–1966) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. He served at the Sumer Public Library, the Archaeological Survey of India, Government Museum Jodhpur, and Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre.

Biswanath Banerjee (1926–2018) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University from 1967 to 1991 and served as president of The Asiatic Society around 2004–2007.

Blain Auer works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He is a professor at the University of Lausanne (attested 2018) and serves on the editorial board of Perspectives on Islamicate South Asia.
Bo Jiang specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman (attested 2008).

Bo Utas (b. 1938) is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University (ca. 1958–1972) under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and Stig Wikander, later holding a post there from around 1987 to 2003.
Bo-Kwang Han is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2004 and 2015).

Bokar Rinpoche (1940–2004) was a master in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kalu Rinpoche from around 1967 to 1989 and was based at Bokar Ngedon Choekhor Ling Monastery from around 1984 to 2004.

Bong Seok Joo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser, also studying with Lewis Lancaster, Ding-hwa E. Hsieh, and Jacqueline Stone.

Bongkil Chung specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and held posts in philosophy at Florida International University (1991–1992, attested 2012).

Boris Turayev (1868–1920) was a historian who studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of St. Petersburg University (ca. 1887–1891). He held a post at the University of Saint Petersburg from around 1898 to 1920.

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov (1900–1981) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1920–1925) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1937).

Boris Vladimirtsov (1884–1931) studied at St. Petersburg University and under Antoine Meillet. He worked in linguistics, history, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, holding posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1918–1931) and the National Library of Russia (1924–1925).
Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima (1898–1959) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Shri Singha Shedra under traditional teachers Tubten Nyendrak and Khenpo Genam.

Boyd Michailovsky is a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology. He held affiliations at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1976–1978) and Langues et civilisations à tradition orale (attested 1990).
